findings.evidence: The factorization proof uses the domain hypothesis through `aeval_additivePolynomial_sub` (AdditivePolynomial.lean:182). Its universal polynomial identity can first be established in the domain K[X] and evaluated in arbitrary L; the splitting proof then only uses this factorization and `Splits.prod`.
findings.fix: State both results with `[CommRing L] [Algebra K L]`. Prove the additive polynomial identity over K[X], then transport it by evaluation to establish factorization and splitting; retain the domain assumption for translation results.
findings.issue: `map_additivePolynomial_sub_C_eq_prod` (line 65) and `splits_additivePolynomial_sub_C` (line 79) unnecessarily require `[IsDomain L]`; both identities hold in any commutative K-algebra containing the root.

summary: Factorization and splitting retain an unnecessary domain assumption, excluding commutative algebras with zero divisors.
